text: Iqra Yousaf, a medical sales officer with a declared monthly income of PKR 150,000, has engaged in a pattern of structuring cash deposits to evade reporting thresholds. Between May 3 and May 28, 2026, she made ten cash deposits totaling approximately PKR 16.9 million across four different branches in Karachi (Clifton, Saddar, Gulshan-e-Iqbal, and DHA Phase 6). Each deposit was deliberately kept below the PKR 2 million Cash Transaction Report (CTR) threshold, ranging from PKR 830,000 to PKR 1.93 million. This activity is highly inconsistent with her low-risk profile and salaried occupation. Furthermore, the funds were rapidly transferred out via RTGS to Al-Noor Exchange Company in four separate transactions totaling PKR 13.9 million, suggesting the account is being used to layer illicit funds through a money changer. On May 16, 2026, the customer explicitly declined to explain the source of the cash when questioned by branch operations about the paperwork requirements for large deposits. The combination of structuring, rapid movement of funds to an exchange company, and refusal to provide source of funds information indicates a high likelihood of money laundering.
